plans: Wire-first reproduction then containment repair: stand up two disposable loopback servers (origin and target) that log method, request URL, Host and body; prove the foreign delivery end to end for both public input forms and a widened spelling set; add an origin-containment rule at both resolution sites so the supplied text is resolved literally under the supplied origin; then run a differential keep/reach matrix on vulnerable and patched copies plus a clean-apply check on a pristine tree.

Parser-table first then one wire confirmation: drive the public entry points and the internal URL-resolution helper with a table of path shapes (ordinary, query-only, protocol-relative, absolute, backslash, userinfo, encoded slashes, same-origin host echo), record the resolved origin and path without sockets, derive the smallest containment rule that maps every resolved origin back to the supplied origin, patch it, re-run the table, and only then perform a single two-server confirmation.

Connection interception: leave the library logic untouched at first and instrument the connector or agent layer to record the actual host and port opened for each caller-supplied path shape, establishing socket-level ground truth independent of URL objects; then apply the repair and replay the same interception map to prove no path shape reaches a foreign socket while controls still connect to the origin.

Differential oracle over a generated path corpus: define a literal-path oracle whose expected request target is the origin host and port plus the supplied path text, generate a corpus of boundary shapes, compare the vulnerable library against the oracle, repair until zero origin-changing shapes remain, then replay the corpus on the patched copy and on a freshly patched pristine tree while treating measured URL normalization as part of the oracle.
